rationale: Compound: ⲣ̄- ('do') + ⲙⲛⲧ- (abstract) + ⲁⲱⲓⲣⲉ/ⲁϩⲓⲣⲉ (probably from ⲟⲩⲱⲓⲉ 'farmer/doer' or related agentive root). Recurring three times on this page (lines 17, 18, 20) as the apostolic activity Paul shares with the earlier apostles — 'I have labored ... my brothers the apostles ... themselves did the labor and laid foundations.' Echoes 1 Cor 15:10 ἐκοπίασα. Given the agricultural metaphors elsewhere in this kephalaion (sowing seed, foundations), 'farmer-work' is a plausible specific reading; 'labor' a safer general one.
Demonstrative ⲡⲓ- + ⲱⲁⲧ. Functions as adjective in 'this ⲱⲁⲧ favor.' May be Lyc. form of ⲛⲟϭ 'great' or related quantifier. Confidence low; flag for parallels.

Apparent dialectal/scribal variant of ⲁⲛⲁⲕ ⲇⲉ 'But I.' Letter-order may reflect a Lycopolitan quirk of this manuscript witness. Functions as standard adversative subject-pronoun construction at the start of the apostolic self-declaration.
Construction in line 15 introducing those just mentioned. Possibly contracted Lyc. for a topicalizing phrase. Function-translated 'as for them.'

Verb governing ⲛⲉⲙⲏⲓ̈ 'with me' and predicating ⲛⲕⲁⲏⲣⲟⲛⲟⲙⲟⲥ 'fellow-heirs.' Likely qualitative of ⲱⲱⲧ 'be joined, be united' with ϩⲁ- prefix functioning future-modally. Captures the unity-of-inheritance imagery (Rom 8:17 συγκληρονόμοι).

Verb in line 1 'in every work to which they ⲉϩⲩⲝⲧ their hand upon it.' The idiom ⲧⲟⲟⲧϥ̄ ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'hand upon' indicates a setting/applying action, but the verbal stem ⲩⲝⲧ is unidentified. Possible candidates: Lyc. reflex of a piercing/stretching/applying verb. Confidence very low.
